name: Real Options Investment Model
description: Perpetual investment-option benchmark reconstructed from Pindyck (1991), pp.1119-1121, equations5-10, and Dixit/Pindyck (1994), chapter5. Here mu is the risk-neutral drift r minus the opportunity cost of waiting. At default mu=r the opportunity cost is zero: no finite exercise threshold exists, the option-value limit is the asset value, and immediate exercise is never optimal. Trigger_Value is an explicit report label in that case; no infinity or false zero enters integration. Option_Value and its delta are the analytic value-matching/smooth-pasting solution, replacing the unrelated intrinsic-value lag stock. Invested is the current source exercise-policy indicator, not an accumulated construction rate; on the saved strictly increasing deterministic asset scenario it is also irreversible. The existing sinusoidal Noise is a deterministic illustration, not a Wiener process or Monte Carlo GBM simulation. Financial calibration and general path-dependent exercise handling are outside this educational benchmark.

variables.name: Trigger_Value
variables.equation: IF(mu == r, 'No finite exercise threshold', IF(mu < r, Investment_Cost * beta / (beta - 1), 'Unbounded perpetual option value'))

variables.name: Option_Value
variables.equation: IF(mu == r, Asset_Value, IF(mu < r, IF(Asset_Value < Investment_Cost * beta / (beta - 1), Investment_Cost / (beta - 1) * (Asset_Value * (beta - 1) / (Investment_Cost * beta))^beta, Asset_Value - Investment_Cost), 1 / 0))

variables.name: Option_Delta
variables.equation: IF(mu == r, 1, IF(mu < r, IF(Asset_Value < Investment_Cost * beta / (beta - 1), (Asset_Value * (beta - 1) / (Investment_Cost * beta))^(beta - 1), 1), 1 / 0))

reference: Pindyck RS (1991). Irreversibility, Uncertainty, and Investment. Journal of Economic Literature29:1110-1148, pp.1119-1121, equations5-10. Dixit/Pindyck (1994), Investment under Uncertainty, chapter5.
